groups.label: Adjective Order (OSASCOMP)
groups.definition: Standard sequence when using multiple adjectives before a noun: Opinion, Size, Age, Shape, Colour, Origin, Material, Purpose.
rules: Opinion -> Size -> Age -> Shape -> Colour -> Origin -> Material -> Purpose + Noun
Example: A beautiful small old round red Italian wooden dining table.

examples.t: A lovely big new black leather jacket.

groups.label: Comparatives & Superlatives
groups.definition: Forming comparative (-er / more) and superlative (-est / most) forms to compare qualities.
rules: 2+ syllables: use 'more' / 'the most' (more expensive -> the most expensive).
Irregulars: good -> better -> best, bad -> worse -> worst, far -> farther -> farthest.

examples.t: This is the most interesting book.

groups.label: Participial Adjectives (-ed vs -ing)
groups.definition: Adjectives ending in -ed describe feelings/internal states; adjectives ending in -ing describe the cause/thing provoking the feeling.
rules: -ed describe human emotional state: I am bored / interested / exhausted.
-ing describe the external cause: The lesson is boring / interesting / exhausting.
